slides.title: Electric Drive Electrical machines
slides.body:
The basic architecture of a motion control system
includes:
1. Electric Source: provides the energy to the
drive system
2. Power Electronic Converter : interfaces the
motor with the power source and provides the
motor with adjustable voltage, current and/or
frequency.
3. Controller: by comparing the input command
for speed and/or position with the actual values
measured through sensors, provides appropriate
control signals to the power converter.
Electric DriveElectrical machines

slides.title: Electric Drive Electrical machines
slides.body:
4. Electric Motor: selected according to the
power level, environmental factors and
performance required by the load.
5. One or more feedback Sensors to return the
position and/or velocity of the actuator to the
motion controller in order to close the position
and/or velocity control loops.
6. Mechanical components to transform the
motion of the actuator into the desired load
motion, including: gears, shafting, ball screw,
belts, linkages, and linear and rotational
bearings.
Electric DriveElectrical machines

slides.title: Electric Motors Electrical machines
slides.body:
An electric motor converts electrical energy to mechanical
energy. It consists in a cylindrical structure with a fixed,
static part, called stator, and a moving, rotating one, the
rotor.
Both the structures can be populated with either windings
or permanent magnets, achieving different electrical and
magnetic performances.
The energy conversion happens in the interaction
between the magnetic fields of the two structures, which
produces a net output torque.
Electric MotorsElectrical machines

In a motor, the induced emf always acts to reduce the current in the loop. That’s why it is called
“back emf.”
In fact, Faraday-Neumann-Lenz law establish that the induced current in a loop is in the direction
that creates a magnetic field that opposes the change in magnetic flux through the area enclosed
by the loop. The induced current tends to keep the original magnetic flux through the circuit from
changing.

slides.title: Pros and Cons DC Machine
slides.body:
Pros:
- Simple operation and motor control
- Cheapest and simplest motor
- Speed proportional to voltage
Cons:
- Requires high maintenance
- Sparking
- Low-life span (due to physical wear on brushes)
DC motor drive technology is very mature and well developed. However, with the ever-increasing
demand on high efficiency, high power density, and maintenance-free operation, DC motor drives are
no longer attractive for EV propulsion.
Pros and ConsDC Machine

slides.title: Structure DC Machine
slides.body:
The stator, external, equipped with salient poles, works as an inductor and
can be realized:
- with excitation windings arranged around the pole bodies; such
windings are crossed by direct current and are connected to each other in
controversial series to generate magnetic polarity of alternating sign from
one pole to the next;
- with permanent magnets.
The internal rotor, consisting of a cylinder of magnetic material, works as
armature; on the periphery of the rotor are uniformly distributed slots where
the active conductors are housed. The set of active conductors (connected in
series with each other) constitutes a closed circuit.
StructureDC Machine

slides.title: Structure DC Machine
slides.body:
The part in the air between stator and rotor is called air gap, in this area the
field magnetic has the greatest intensity.
The commutator is mounted on the same shaft as the rotor. This is for the
purpose of supply the windings with the power supply voltage and ensure
that the torque generated by the current that passes through is constant or at
least unidirectional.
The brushes crawl on the collector and electrically connect it to the external
terminals of the machine.
The presence of the system commutator-brushes causes various issues,
mainly the continuous maintenance required and the undesired sparking.
StructureDC Machine

slides.title: Basic principle Inverter
slides.body:
The inverter design highly depends on the technology of power
devices. Nowadays, the insulated-gate bipolar transistor
(IGBT)-based inverter is most attractive and has been widely
accepted by modern EVs.
The selection of power devices is based on:
- the voltage rating is at least twice the nominal battery
voltage;
- the current rating is large enough so that there is no need
to connect several power devices in parallel;
- the switching speed is sufficiently high to suppress motor
harmonics and acoustic noise.
Basic principleInverter

slides.title: Basic principle Inverter
slides.body:
Inverters for Induction or Permanent Magnet motors are
generally classified into voltage-fed and current-fed types.
Because of the need of a large series inductance to emulate a
current source, the current-fed inverters are rarely used for EV
propulsion.
In fact, the voltage-fed inverters are almost exclusively used
because they are very simple and can have power flow in
either direction.
Control strategies can be classified as:
- PWM (Pulse Width Modulation);
- Six-step.
Basic principleInverter

slides.title: Six-step Control Inverter
slides.body:
In 6-step (or square wave) operation, the switch is alternately
closed and open for a time equal to T/2, where T is the period of
the alternating output voltage.
The switches of the same branch are controlled in a
complementary way.
Six-step ControlInverter

slides.title: Six-step Control Inverter
slides.body:
In 6-step operation, each switch changes state every T/2, while the
inverter changes state every T/6.
It is called a 6-step inverter since the waveform is built in the 6
sixths of the period. Every sixth of a period, the components that
are commanded for switching change.
Furthermore, in period T the inverter assumes 6 different states:
(101), (100), (110), (010), (011), (001). These are called active
states.
The amplitude of the output voltage depends only on V CC and the
state of the switches.
Six-step ControlInverter

slides.title: Overview Induction Machine
slides.body:
o Commutatorless motor drives offer a number of advantages over conventional DC motor drives
for electric propulsion, as low cost, high power factor, reliable operation.
o An AC induction motor is one of the simplest and most reliable types of electric AC motor, with
the power ranging from a few watts to many kilowatts.
o There are many different ways to design and control such motors, from low cost with a single-
phase input to high accuracy with a polyphase approach, and this type of system is the most
widely used motor across the consumer and industrial markets.
OverviewInduction Machine

slides.title: The most common type of IMs is the squirrel- cage IM. It consists of: ● a stator incorporated with three-phase armature
Working principle Induction Machine
slides.body:
The stator of a three-phase induction machine contains a series of
windings to which three-phase electrical power is applied.
These windings establish a rotating magnetic field in the air gap
between the stator and the rotor.
The stator field can be seen as a series of north-south poles
revolving around the circumference of the stator.
The rotation of the stator magnetic field occurs at a fixed speed
called synchronous speed and linked to the supply frequency f.
In IMs, the angular speed of the rotor is lower than the
synchronous speed of the magnetic field generated by the stator
windings, hence called asynchronous.
Working principleInduction Machine

slides.title: Working principle Induction Machine
slides.body:
The rotor windings are immersed in this rotating magnetic
field. Since the rotor turns slower than the stator field, the
magnetic flux linkage in the rotor windings varies.
The rotating magnetic field induces currents in the rotor
by magnetic induction (Faraday's law).
These induced currents, in turn, generate a rotor
magnetic field, which opposes flux variations; it interacts
with the stator field, generating a torque on the rotor
windings which causes the rotor to rotate.
Working principleInduction Machine

slides.title: Modeling Induction Machine
Torque Induction Machine
slides.body:
At synchronous speed, no torque is produced by the
motor, because no current is induced in the rotor windings.
If the rotor rotates at a lower speed than the stator field, the
motor runs in motoring mode.
Otherwise, the motor operates in generator mode. The
maximum torque, which can be obtained at the motor shaft,
is called pullout torque.
The nominal torque is conventionally half of the pullout
torque.
The motor usually operates in the linear region between
the positive and the negative nominal torque.

slides.title: Squirrel cage Induction Machine
slides.body:
Because of high cost, need for maintenance, and lack of
sturdiness, the wound-rotor induction motor is less attractive than
the squirrel-cage counterpart, especially for electric propulsion in
electric vehicles (EVs). Hence, the squirrel-cage induction motor
is loosely named as the induction motor for EV propulsion.
In addition to the common advantages of commutatorless motor
drives, the induction motor drives possess the definite advantages
of low cost and ruggedness. These advantages can generally
outweigh their major disadvantage of control complexity and
facilitate this technology being widely accepted for EVs.
Squirrel cageInduction Machine

slides.title: o o o Overview PM Brushless
slides.body:
o Among various types of motor drives, permanent magnet (PM) brushless motor drives,
especially the PM synchronous motor drive, are currently the most attractive motor drives for
electric vehicle (EV) propulsion.
o Their key features, namely high power density and high efficiency, are attributed to the use
of high-energy PM material. Actually, they are becoming dominant in the market share of EV
motor drives. However, these PM brushless motor drives still have some shortcomings such as
high cost and thermal instability of the PM material.
o The family of PM brushless machines has two main members: the PM synchronous machine
and the PM BLDC machine . The PM synchronous machine has been widely used for EV
propulsion; meanwhile, the PM BLDC machine is becoming attractive.
OverviewPM Brushless

slides.title: Classification PM Brushless
slides.body:
Brushless synchronous motors can be categorized as follows according to the shape of the back emf developed at
the air gap:
● Trapezoidal, the machine is powered by CSI inverter, BLDC (Brushless DC) machine;
● Sinusoidal, the machine is powered by VSI inverters with sinusoidal voltages (PMSM).
ClassificationPM Brushless

slides.title: Structure PM Brushless
slides.body:
The basic structure of the PM brushless machine, including
both the PMSM and BLDC types, consists of:
● a stator housing a winding, typically three-phase
connected in a star, through which the motor itself is
powered;
● a rotor equipped with permanent magnets capable of
establishing a magnetic field in the air gap quite similar to
that produced by the excitation winding placed on the
rotor of normal synchronous motors.
Compared with the induction machine, it is relatively simpler
because of the absence of cage bars and end-rings.
StructurePM Brushless

slides.title: Working principle PMSM
slides.body:
In the machine, the rotor rotates at the same speed as
the rotating magnetic field of the stator, so the mechanical
speed of the rotor coincides with the synchronous speed.
The principle of PM synchronous machine is based on the
interaction of sinusoidal back electromotive force
(EMF) waveforms and sinusoidal armature (stator)
current waveforms.
Working principlePMSM

slides.title: Working principle BLDC
slides.body:
The principle of a BLDC machine is based on the
interaction of trapezoidal back EMF waveforms and
rectangular armature current waveforms.
BLDC motors are also referred to as electronically
commutated motor. As with mechanical commutation,
the electronic commutation helps in achieving
unidirectional torque similar to a conventional DC
machine.
Working principleBLDC

slides.title: Modeling BLDC
slides.body:
In a BLDC machine the back EMF waveforms are
trapezoidal, rather than sinusoidal. Thus, the d–q
modeling technique developed for the PM
synchronous machine is not applicable. Since the flux
linkage is nonsinusoidal, it is necessary to derive the
model of the PM brushless machine in terms of its
state variables.
ModelingBLDC

slides.title: Working principle SRM
slides.body:
The Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) is an electric motor that
runs by reluctance torque.
The rotor has no magnets or coils attached. It is a solid salient-
pole rotor made of soft magnetic material.
When power is applied to the stator windings, the rotor’s
magnetic reluctance creates a force that attempts to align the
rotor pole with the nearest stator pole.
In order to maintain rotation, an electronic control system
switches on the windings of successive stator poles in sequence
so that magnetic field of the stator leads the rotor pole, pulling it
forward.
Working principleSRM

slides.title: FOC Control strategies
slides.body:
Another control strategy for inverter-fed variable-speed drives is the “Field Oriented Control” (FOC).
The time-dependent instantaneous three-phase system values, such as currents and voltages, are
transformed into an orthogonal two-dimensional coordinate system by means of the Park transformation.
This coordinate system rotates with the same frequency as the three-phase values.
From this, the three AC quantities are reduced to two DC quantities which, in general, are much
simpler to control. The two DC quantities can be represented as a “space vector” in the two-dimensional
coordinate system. This transformation results in a controllability of torque of the induction machine that
is similar to the DC machine.
FOCControl strategies

With this type of regulation it is possible to
obtain rapid response and good adaptation
by the machine, whose operation, moreover, can
be extended to the four quadrants.

slides.title: Outcome Lessons
slides.body:
Among the three main types of commercially available EV motor drives, namely the DC, induction,
and PM brushless, the PM brushless motor drives take the definite advantages of higher
efficiency, higher power density, and higher torque density, which are highly desirable for EV
propulsion. Currently, there is no doubt that the PM brushless motor drives are the preferred
technology for EVs.
Between the two members of PM brushless motor drives, the PM synchronous motor drive is
more mature than the PM BLDC motor drive while they have their individual merits. That is, the
PM synchronous motor drive has relatively higher efficiency and lower torque ripple, whereas
the PM BLDC motor drive has relatively higher power density and higher torque density.
